text: hunter-s27b/heavy-reach-has-a-hard-100px-floor records its one remaining unknown as 'the base value 1t4420s0 ... which is set elsewhere and which I did not resolve'. It resolves. Web: 1t99s0.as:105 initialises 1t4420s0 to 10, :194 assigns it from the tenth initPlayer parameter, and :223 halves it ('*= 0.5') in one branch. The android twin is positionally identical - MCSPlayer.as:107 'internal var baseSlashLength:int = 10;', :182 declares initPlayer with baseSlashLength as its tenth parameter, :193 assigns it, :222 halves it - which names 1t4420s0 = baseSlashLength. The value fed in, for NPCs, is computed by the caller: EnemyElite.as:102 baseSlashLength = 120 + floor(90 * speed / (20 + speed)), i.e. a saturating curve from 120 px at speed 0 toward 210 px, 165 px at speed 20. So reach = baseSlashLength x per-stance multiplier, and at the low end the 100 px heavy floor genuinely bites: base 120 at mastery 0 gives 60, clamped up to 100. CAVEAT, stated plainly: the formula line is android v0.682, so under S0-3/C2 it is v0.682 until a web caller is read; what IS web-attested is that the base is an injected per-fighter slash length with a halving branch, not a global constant. Two further web stance cases the original finding did not list: 1t99s0.as:3131 (Dual) = base * 1.4 and :3142 (Reversed) = base * 1.0.

lane_impact: Gauntlet tooling: reduces false QUOTE_UNVERIFIED flags across every remaining packet. NOT applied - this lane is forbidden to modify files outside its journal.
text: Both QUOTE_UNVERIFIED claims in this packet had byte-exact quotes, and they are the only two claims in the packet that delimited their quotes with BACKTICKS instead of straight or curly quotes. citeLint's QUOTED_SPAN_RE recognises only double quotes, curly quotes and single quotes - a backticked span never becomes a candidate, so the check falls back to 6-word shingles and long tokens, which in this corpus straddle the ' · ' separators and the 'file.as:NNNN' prefixes and land nowhere. I re-ran the five affected lines as exact string comparisons after strip(): §1t99s0§.as:249, :3050, :3060, :3272 and :3274 all match their quoted text character for character. This is worth fixing because the packet's instruction makes QUOTE_UNVERIFIED the top-priority refute target, so a purely cosmetic delimiter choice is currently steering critics toward refuting sound claims - the exact over-refutation failure mode §0 warns about. Adding a backtick alternative to QUOTED_SPAN_RE is a one-token fix.

text: A live S0-3 / C2 parity datum nobody has claimed, and it is the reason the '271 cap' number is safe to ship for the WEB build only. The two builds carry DIFFERENT stat ceilings and different per-point grants. Web v0.717 §1t5957s0§.as:3340-3346: level into _loc2_, then HP < 10 + (lvl+10)*10, Chi < 10 + (lvl+10)*5, AP < 30 + (lvl+10)*5, ATK/DEF/SPD < 1 + (lvl+10)*3 — giving 271 for ATK at level 80. Android v0.682 InventoryUI.as:2406-2412: charlevel from getStat(STAT_LEVEL), then HP < 10 + (charlevel+10)*5, Chi < 10 + (charlevel+10)*5, AP < 20 + (charlevel+10), ATK/DEF/SPD < charlevel + 10 — giving 90 for ATK at level 80, and the android HP ceiling is HALF the web one. The android add-handler at :2416-2419 grants +5 MAXHP per point against the web build's implied +10. So RR:199's 'Ready: ... +10HP ... per point' and the whole 271 figure are v0.717 values that the android data XMLs cannot be used to corroborate.

text: A measured, first-hand web-vs-android divergence in the SAME meter, which is the cleanest counterexample I found to treating the android decompile as a stand-in for v0.717. The web player initialises its focus maximum to 8 * 24 = 192 with the current value at 0; the android twin initialises maxreload to 5 * 24 = 120 with reload at 0. Same function position, same init sequence (both immediately followed by the HUD update call), different constant. Every ratio-based port between the two builds must be rescaled by 192/120, and the web's stance toll of 48 is 25% of the bar while the android's threshold of maxreload/6 = 20 is 16.7% of its own.

lane_impact: L5 combat-core: CRIT_MULT = 1.3 is CONDITIONAL on a full 192/192 Focus bar, not probabilistic. Also explains why 20+ video samples never yielded a crit RATE — there isn't one.
text: The 1.3x multiplier that the ledger discusses as a crit is not rolled — it is a full-meter condition, deterministic. The damage function's tail at §1t99s0§.as:3272-3274 tests focus == maxfocus and returns the stanced damage times 1.3 plus a flat bonus term. No Math.random anywhere in that branch. Combined with the 48-per-switch toll (:3162) and the slash costs (:3302-3310) this makes Focus a single resource with a sharp cliff at the top: the bonus exists ONLY at exactly 192/192, so any spend at all removes it, and the same full-bar condition gates two other abilities (:3383, :3707). That is a very different feel from a percentage crit chance and would be trivially wrong to seed as one.
